name: IEC AND dependency (G)
summary: Dependency label Gm: inputs or outputs carrying the number m are ANDed with the affecting G input.
description: In dependency notation, an input labelled G followed by a number is an affecting input. Every input or output labelled with the same number is ANDed with it. When the G input is at its internal 1 state the affected signals act normally; at its internal 0 state they are forced to 0. A bar over the number means the complement of the G input affects them.

G dependency lets a device symbol show gating relationships without drawing extra AND gates. It is common on multiplexers, gated clocks and register symbols in device data books, and a drafter copying such a symbol must keep the numbers intact or the meaning changes.
The label describes logic only. It does not tell you whether the gating causes glitches on a clock line or what setup time applies between G and the affected input.
readingNotes: Match each G number to every input or output carrying that number.
A bar over the affected number means the complement of G applies.
drawingChecklist: Keep G numbers unique within a symbol.
Label every affected terminal with the matching number.
Avoid mixing G numbers with other dependency letters using the same number.
distinction: V (OR) dependency imposes a 1 state when the affecting input is 1; G imposes a 0 state when the affecting input is 0.
